issue_title: Kmeans integer arithmetic can choose the wrong nearest centroid
pr_title: Avoid integer overflow in Kmeans distance calculations
issue_body:
### Description

`Kmeans` subtracts and squares integer samples and integer centroids before converting the result to floating point. These operations overflow in the original integer dtype and can change both training assignments and predictions.

```python
import numpy as np
from mlxtend.cluster import Kmeans

model = Kmeans(k=2, random_seed=0).fit(
    np.array([[0], [200]], dtype=np.uint8)
)
print(model.predict(np.array([[25], [75], [125], [175]], dtype=np.uint8)))
# Current:  [1, 0, 1, 0]
# Expected: [1, 1, 0, 0] (centroid order is [200, 0])
```

A real first Lloyd step on int8 samples `[[0], [1], [99], [100]]` with `k=2, max_iter=1, random_seed=0` also produces centroids `[[50], [50]]` instead of the floating-input result `[[100/3], [100]]`.

### Proposed change and verification

Promote distance arithmetic to at least float64 before subtraction and squaring, retaining wider floating-point dtypes. Keep the input arrays unchanged.

On master `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`, 18 new dtype/regression/control cases produce 6 failures and 12 passes. Predictions use an independent Python-integer distance reference; training is compared with the same real Lloyd step on float64 samples. The fixed candidate passes all 69 cluster and base-model tests.

[Completed reproduction and validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43665368984).
pr_body:
### Description

Integer `Kmeans` samples and centroids are subtracted and squared in their original dtype. Overflow can select a farther centroid and change the Lloyd update. For example, uint8 queries 75 and 125 are assigned to the wrong side of centroids 0 and 200; an int8 first update can collapse two centroids to 50 instead of producing 100/3 and 100.

Promote the centroids once per assignment pass to the combined input/centroid dtype with at least float64 precision. Subtraction and squaring then use floating arithmetic, while wider floating-point inputs keep their precision. No input array is changed.

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`. Validated source: `e319582813845e455ecdbf7173ae767d22ccd1f3`.

- The same 18 new cases give **6 failures and 12 passes on unchanged production source**.
- With the fix, **69 cluster and base-model tests pass**.
- Cases cover int8/uint8/int16/uint16/int32/uint32/int64 and float32/float64 controls. Actual predictions are checked against Python-integer squared distances; actual first-step centroids and memberships are compared with the same data in float64.
- Input preservation, existing three-blob clustering and continued-fitting tests pass.
- Changed-file Black, isort and Flake8 checks pass. The workflow verifies a clean source checkout after restoring the baseline test.
- Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, using the frozen uv development environment on Ubuntu. The full repository suite was not run.

[Successful validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43665368984). An earlier run passed the tests but failed test-file formatting; the linked run verifies the corrected exact commit.

### Related work

Reviewed all previous Afloat16 PRs, relevant all-state upstream searches and the Kmeans source at all 34 pre-existing fork branch heads. All retain the original integer distance calculation. The earlier empty-cluster branch changes mean recomputation only.
